title: Proposal for Review of Operational Risks with Consolidation of RSAF's Assets in Fewer Airbases
what_it_is: Proposal for Review of Operational Risks with Consolidation of RSAF's Assets in Fewer Airbases

sections.label: SAF intelligence, airbases, resilience
sections.summary: Singapore requires robust intelligence, hardened infrastructure, dispersed assets and reserve capacity, with Tengah, Changi and Pulau Sudong airbase investments supporting the Paya Lebar relocation.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Broadly speaking, our circumstances require us to have a robust intelligence and effective threat detection and early warning systems at range, so that the SAF can mount timely and decisive responses with a suite of diversified capabilities across multiple layers and distances where necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For this reason, our critical infrastructures and facilities are hardened against potential attacks, and our key assets can be dispersed in peace time and especially during contingencies.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have also factored in reserve capacities to ensure resilience for scenarios where some of our assets may be destroyed or damaged.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The decision to relocate Paya Lebar Air Base to free up land for national development purposes was a carefully considered one, taking into account the factors I have just mentioned, as well as then-emerging and now-evolving threats.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: For example, in terms of available airbases and runways, we have invested significant resources in expanding Tengah Air Base and Changi Air Base, and lengthening the contingency runway at Pulau Sudong.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Tengah Air Base and Changi Air Base are also being upgraded with better detection, response and resilience capabilities, including against the emerging threats posed by drones.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Public Services and Minister for Defence (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The SAF will continually assess our operational, infrastructure and capability requirements, taking into consideration the threats on the horizon and available technologies, while carefully weighing the costs and risks to Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore's geography and strike risk
sections.summary: Singapore's lack of hinterland or depth makes the risk of any strike on it always very high, shaping its unique operational concepts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, I have said that based on our geography, the risk of any strike on Singapore is always very high because we lack hinterland or depth – which is why our operational concepts are quite unique for our own operational needs.
